Stormont, Belfast The five seats won (out of a possible 78) represented 10.1% of the vote. This was seen as a triumph for Sinn Féin and their new policy. Sinn Féin’s new political presence was also felt in Westminster when Gerry Adams won the West Belfast seat in the 1983 general election. Although just one seat, this represented 13.4% of the vote in Northern Ireland. 1983 was also the year in which Gerry Adams became the President of Sinn Féin. ABSTENTION To further their political aims, at the 1986 Ard Fheis Sinn Féin decided to end its policy of abstention (a refusal to take seats that are won in an election) from Dáil Éireann (the lower house of the Irish Parliament). The decision to end this policy led to a split in Sinn Féin, with a number of members leaving to form Republican Sinn Féin.
